lead.event: Singapore passes Digital Infrastructure Bill covering major data centres
lead.headline: Singapore passes Digital Infrastructure Bill for data centres with 3MW IT load
lead.blurb: Parliament passed the law on 7 October, setting licensing thresholds at a critical IT load of at least 3 megawatts, 10MW for major co-location and cloud data centres, or S$100 million in average annual revenue from Singapore users over the preceding three years for major cloud providers. Existing and new data centres must meet facility-level energy-efficiency requirements, including power usage effectiveness standards, while major operators will face cyber-incident reporting and business-continuity requirements. Breaches of cybersecurity and business-continuity requirements may draw fines of up to S$1 million or 10 per cent of annual Singapore turnover, whichever is higher.

deals_control.event: IOI Properties and CapitaLand pursue One Raffles Place acquisition
deals_control.headline: IOI Properties, CapitaLand Investment pursue One Raffles Place at S$2.3 billion-S$2.4 billion
deals_control.blurb: Their joint offer gives each a 50% share, and the partners are in exclusive due diligence and ongoing negotiations with the owners. OUE REIT said no binding agreement has been signed and the transaction may not materialise.

deals_control.event: IOI Properties to acquire Shenton 101 from its CEO's vehicle
deals_control.headline: IOI Properties agrees to acquire Shenton 101 from CEO’s vehicle for one dollar
deals_control.blurb: The vehicle belongs to group CEO and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng and holds Shenton House. IOI Properties will settle about 217.6 million dollars in shareholder advances and consolidate about 376.23 million dollars in borrowings, both as at 31 July, with completion targeted for 4Q2026 subject to approvals and consents.

deals_control.event: CDL unveils S$6 billion divestment and S$5 billion reinvestment strategy
deals_control.headline: CDL unveils S$6 billion divestment and S$5 billion reinvestment plan
deals_control.blurb: The plan targets mainly commercial and hospitality properties in the UK, China and Australia, with an orderly exit from nearly all of its Australian presence except hospitality. New investments are allocated 60%-30%-10% to Singapore, China and Japan, and CDL aims to double assets under management to S$10 billion by FY2029.

deals_control.event: Far East Orchard raises its stake in FEHT's managers
deals_control.headline: Far East Orchard raises stake in FEHT managers to 75%
deals_control.blurb: It will pay S$28.3 million in cash for an additional 42% stake in the two management entities, becoming FEHT’s main sponsor. The deal is expected to lift assets under management by about 86% to S$3.9 billion and deliver 3.7% pro-forma earnings-per-share accretion. It is slated to close by the end of 2026 and does not require shareholder approval.

macro_flows.event: Singapore retail property transactions reach S$7.38 billion year to date
macro_flows.headline: Singapore retail property transactions reach S$7.38 billion year to date
macro_flows.blurb: As of 22 September, the total was nearly double 2025’s full-year S$3.75 billion and 44.6% above the 2022 peak of S$5.1 billion. The S$3.9 billion Paragon sale was the year’s largest deal. Analysts cite improved retail fundamentals and net yields of 4% to 5%, but warn further US rate hikes could slow large transactions.

macro_flows.event: Singapore bank sell-off follows analyst warnings and earnings concerns
macro_flows.headline: Singapore bank sell-off deepens as OCBC falls 3.86%
macro_flows.blurb: Citi Research cut OCBC to sell from neutral with a S$27.50 target, citing expected flat year-on-year third-quarter earnings. DBS and UOB also fell as investors weighed earnings risks and profit-taking. A Phillip Securities manager expected strong quarterly results in early November and about 10 per cent loan growth.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Mi Material files prospectus for Singapore IPO
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: Mi Material files Singapore IPO prospectus to raise S$168.2 million
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: The offer comprises 51.5 million new shares and 26 million vendor shares at S$1.80 each, with cornerstone investors subscribing for 41.9 million shares. Mi Material expects to list on 28 October at a target market capitalisation of about S$891 million, while Mi Technovation will retain roughly 73.7%.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Geo Energy conducts share buyback and expands coal production target
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: Geo Energy raises 2027 coal target to 17–19 million tonnes, buys back 6 million shares
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: The 6 million-share repurchase cost S$3.6 million, at about 60 cents per share, roughly 11% above July’s average. Geo Energy reaffirmed its 3Q 2026 profit outlook and may use special dividends alongside regular payouts, after returning S$12.1 million to shareholders in 2026.

market_structure_policy.event: SGX reduces board-lot sizes for 11 stocks
market_structure_policy.headline: SGX cuts minimum trade sizes for 11 stocks from 100 units
market_structure_policy.blurb: From 5 October, minimum lots fell to 10 units for stocks in the lower price band and to one unit in the higher band. More than 20,000 10-share trades were executed on the first day, and around 55% of trades across the 11 stocks were below the previous 100-unit lot.

earnings_guidance.event: Macquarie downgrades Jardine Matheson Southeast Asia
earnings_guidance.headline: Macquarie downgrades Jardine Matheson Southeast Asia, cuts target to S$23.50
earnings_guidance.blurb: Macquarie lowered its 12-month target 10% from S$26 and changed its rating from neutral. Shares fell 6.6% to S$27.38 on 7 October after a roughly 10% rally the previous day. Factoring in the Cycle & Carriage unit sale expected in Q1 2027 and a 0.5% Toyota stake distribution, it cut 2027 and 2028 net earnings estimates by 7% and 8%.

earnings_guidance.event: Maybank downgrades Sheng Siong to Hold and cuts earnings forecasts
earnings_guidance.headline: Maybank downgrades Sheng Siong to Hold, cuts earnings forecasts by 1% to 3%
earnings_guidance.blurb: Analyst Hussaini Saifee lowered his target price to S$3.12 from S$3.22, citing weaker policy support, slower expansion and rising competition. He cut planned 2028 supermarket openings to four from five, while shares fell 4.21% to S$2.96 by 11:30am on 9 October.

earnings_guidance.event: OCBC Research initiates EGP Energy coverage with a Buy rating
earnings_guidance.headline: OCBC Research initiates EGP Energy coverage with Buy rating and SGD1.05 target
earnings_guidance.blurb: Analyst Heidi Mo set the target price at SGD1.05 using a 16.5x target P/E, implying 43% upside from the SGD0.77 share price. EGP Energy’s SGD296.2 million order book, equal to 4.8 times FY25 revenue, is expected to drive average annual growth of 36% from FY25 to FY28E.
